block.title: Rocq spends most of Hello’s cold interface build loading imports
block.p: On swa, a cold rq open of hello_never_panics builds 1,092 glibc interfaces. With twelve jobs it took 159.8 s to reach the theorem. Each file starts a fresh Rocq compiler that loads its imports. Together the compilers spent 789 of 1,082 worker-seconds on Require and Load commands.

To account for the wall time, we traced the last interface to finish back through the last prerequisite to finish at each step. Along that chain, Rocq spent 90.8 s loading imports and 26.6 s on the rest of compilation. Another 40.3 s elapsed between an interface becoming ready and its compiler starting. Opening the proof and preparing the build took 2.1 s in total.

A separate system-call trace shows what one process loads to build its interface. GetoptLongPfxSet read 57.6 MiB from 559 compiled input files and wrote a 17 KiB interface. Only 8.4 MiB of those reads came from glibc. Later, HelloStartWp read 115.0 MiB from 1,564 compiled inputs. The filesystem cache was warm for both traces. CPU samples from both compilers showed time in OCaml allocation, deserialization and map updates.

The longest chain by compile time contains 49 getopt files followed by 25 Hello files. The slowest single compilation, HelloImageCpu, took 31.4 s and finished 62 s before the build ended, on a different branch. The 25 Hello files on the longest chain account for most of the earlier functor refactor’s cold-load saving. Their combined compile time, estimated from the original build logs and output timestamps, fell from 55.3 to 44.8 s. The full chain fell from 124.3 to 112.4 s.

tr.td: Ready files ranked by remaining chain
Make goals reordered by chain length

block.p: The scheduling experiment used timings from the earlier run to put the ready file with the longest remaining chain first. This cut queue time on the chain that finished last from 40.3 to 1.1 s. Its compilation time rose from 117.4 to 126.6 s. Reordering the goals passed to Make alone left the open time at 159 seconds. All four safety-theorem builds produced the same set of interfaces and reached the named proof. The smaller hello_libs opening needed 176 interfaces. Their compilers spent 92 of 123 worker-seconds loading imports.

Each row records one run on the same machine with Rocq 9.3, a fresh glibc interface cache, prebuilt Nanofil and Iris libraries, and a warm filesystem cache. Rocq timed each source command and skipped opaque proof bodies under -vos.
